solutionSql:
SELECT s.customer_id,
       i.id,
       SUM(i.amount) OVER (
         PARTITION BY s.customer_id
         ORDER BY i.issued_at, i.id
         ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
       ) AS running_total
FROM invoices i
JOIN shipments s ON s.id = i.shipment_id
ORDER BY s.customer_id, i.issued_at, i.id;

rules.howSolved: The window ORDER BY is issued_at then invoices.id, both ascending, and the outer ORDER BY repeats that order within each customer.
The frame ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW makes the running sum include the current invoice.

notes: Sample returns 205 rows, boundary 154, precision 154. A correlated SUM formulation gives 0 differences on all three datasets.
